intro: I am a computational social scientist studying how AI and algorithmic systems shape the information environments people encounter. I ask how these environments can be redesigned to expand access to trustworthy information while limiting exposure to untrustworthy sources, to represent a broader range of information and perspectives, and to support an informed citizenry.
My work is organized around three themes:

callout.label: Dissertation
callout.text: Leveraging AI-Mediated Information Environments for Democracy

themes.title: Access: Changing the Costs of Information
themes.summary: Making untrustworthy sources harder to reach and trustworthy sources easier to reach.
themes.description: Do democratic outcomes improve when information environments make untrustworthy sources harder to reach and trustworthy sources easier to reach?

subthemes.title: Limiting Exposure to Untrustworthy Sources
subthemes.description: Testing environmental changes, such as muting, against cognitive ones, such as media literacy, for the users who engage most with untrustworthy sources.

items.title: Mercury: data-collection and intervention pipeline for the muting field experiment

subthemes.title: Facilitating Access to Trusted Information
subthemes.description: Testing whether conversational access to official election information improves voter trust, knowledge, and beliefs about elections.

items.title: Evaluating Accuracy and Safety of Election Chatbot
items.authors: Megan Lu, Vashawn Robinson, Ryan Yu, Lina Romero-Fabian, Johnny Zhu, Do Won Kim, Giovanni Luca Ciampaglia, Cody Buntain

themes.title: Representation: Broadening Information and Political Encounters
themes.summary: Broadening the information and political encounters available to citizens.
themes.description: Can information environments broaden the information and encounters available to citizens, so that their views of the world and of one another are less narrow or distorted? I focus on information, perspectives, and encounters that existing environments omit or underrepresent.

subthemes.title: Creating Unexpected Partisan Encounters
subthemes.description: Using AI conversations that challenge partisan expectations to reduce polarization without persuasion.

subthemes.title: Designing Feeds Beyond Engagement
subthemes.description: What drives engagement often diverges from what users value. I design feeds that better align with the stated preferences of users and foster civil engagement across divides.

subthemes.title: Scholarly Information Environments
subthemes.description: Science has its own information environment, where the same questions apply: what gets seen, by whom, and through which systems. I study whose knowledge becomes visible across linguistic divides, and which infrastructures shape how research is found and shared.

themes.title: Informed Citizenry: Supporting Political Learning and Participation
themes.summary: Helping citizens learn about politics and make informed electoral choices.
themes.description: How do citizens learn about politics, process political information, and make electoral choices? And how can information environments, including AI, support more informed participation?

subthemes.title: Political Learning with AI
subthemes.description: Comparing direct exposure to political information, AI-generated summaries, and conversational AI assistance to test whether different forms of AI mediation improve how citizens understand a complex policy issue.
